# Profiles: the rules

A game picks an `audience` and a `channel`. The validator enforces these rules; QA checks the rest in a browser.

## Audiences

### `ages-2-5` — Toddlers and preschoolers (2–5)

Children who do not read yet. Everything is pictures and voice.

- Touch targets ≥ 64 px; tap targets radius ≥ 38 px; child-directed: yes
- No text is needed to play: pictures, sound and voice only (words on screen only supplement the voice).
- No losing, no lives, no timers, no negative feedback.
- Touch targets ≥ 64 dp; tap targets ≥ 76 dp across (radius ≥ 38).
- One tap, instant reward. No swipes, long presses or double taps.
- Multitouch never breaks the game: several fingers at once are normal.
- No flashing: at most 3 flashes per second, no sharp full-screen brightness changes.
- Soft sounds; sound and voice can be switched off by a grown-up.
- Settings, purchases and external links only behind a parent gate.

### `ages-6-8` — Early readers (6–8)

Children who read simple words.

- Touch targets ≥ 48 px; tap targets radius ≥ 28 px; child-directed: yes
- Text needed to play at most at a Grade 2 reading level.
- Mistakes are gentle (a shake, try again); no punishing failure.
- Touch targets ≥ 48 dp.
- Settings, purchases and external links only behind a parent gate.

### `ages-9-12` — Older children (9–12)

Children who read fluently.

- Touch targets ≥ 48 px; tap targets radius ≥ 24 px; child-directed: yes
- Touch targets ≥ 48 dp (Android accessibility guideline).
- Settings, purchases and external links only behind a parent gate.

### `general` — General audience (13+)

Teens and adults. Not child-directed.

- Touch targets ≥ 48 px; tap targets radius ≥ 24 px; child-directed: no
- Touch targets ≥ 48 dp (Android accessibility guideline).

## Channels

### `android-families` — Google Play, Families (child-directed)

Android app on Google Play for a child audience: Families policy, COPPA, AdMob with child-directed settings.

- Platform: android; ads: admob; purchases: yes; privacy policy: required
- Ad limits (floors): no ads in the first 60 s; first after round 2; then at most once per 2 rounds and per 90 s
- Interstitial ads only in the natural break after a round; never during play or at round start.
- No ads in the first 60 s, not before the end of round 2, at most once per 2 rounds and per 90 s.
- AdMob with tagForChildDirectedTreatment, tagForUnderAgeOfConsent, rating G, non-personalized.
- No advertising ID (AD_ID) and no Privacy Sandbox permissions: the merged manifest may contain only the allowlisted permissions (checked after every Android build).
- No banners, no rewarded ads; display-only interstitials recommended (closable within 5 s).
- Purchases and external links only behind the parent gate.
- A privacy policy URL is required (https).
- Each game needs something of its own (mechanic, content, listing): the Repetitive Content policy bans near-identical apps.

### `android` — Google Play (general audience)

Android app on Google Play, not child-directed.

- Platform: android; ads: admob (needs a consent flow — not available yet); purchases: yes; privacy policy: required
- Ad limits (floors): no ads in the first 30 s; first after round 1; then at most once per 2 rounds and per 60 s
- Ads need a GDPR consent flow (Google UMP) — not in the platform yet: turn ads off (`monetization.ads.enabled: false`) until it is.
- A privacy policy URL is required (https).

### `crazygames` — CrazyGames (web portal, 13+)

HTML5 game on CrazyGames: the portal brings the players, pays a share of ad revenue, and needs its SDK for gameplay events and ads.

- Platform: web; ads: portal; purchases: no; privacy policy: optional
- Ad limits (floors): no ads in the first 180 s; first after round 3 or after 300 s of the session, whichever comes first; then at most once per 1 rounds and per 180 s
- Content must be PEGI 12 compliant; the audience is teens and adults (kids games go to the separate kids site — not supported yet).
- The SDK gets loadingStart/loadingStop, gameplayStart/gameplayStop (on every break: menu, result, pause, ad, hidden tab) and happytime — the platform sends them automatically from the round lifecycle.
- Midgame ads only in natural breaks on the way into the next round (death, level end → Play again), never during play and never on a navigational button (menu, home, settings, shop): the casual kit shows them when the player taps Play again, at most once per round and per 3 minutes, not in the first 3 minutes, and the first one at the end of round 3 or after 5 minutes of the session, whichever comes first.
- Rewarded ads only when the player chooses one (a button that says what they get), the reward is always given after a finished ad, and nothing in the game requires watching one. `host.rewarded()` (kit: code) refuses an ad that doesn't follow the player's tap.
- The upload is one file: `gp build --target crazygames` folds the build into games/<id>/upload/index.html (the form takes files, not archives). Initial download ≤ 50 MB, ≤ 20 MB for the mobile homepage (the platform holds games to 20 MB); ≤ 1500 files, ≤ 250 MB in all; relative paths only.
- Basic Launch (the first 7–21 days) has CrazyGames monetization off: every ad request fails. The game must not freeze and must not show reward buttons that do nothing (`host.rewardedAvailable` turns false once ads are off for the session (Basic Launch, an ad blocker) or after two failed ads in a row; `gp qa` checks it). Full Launch also requires that it works with an ad blocker.
- Originality is reviewed: `concept` in game.yaml (E_CONCEPT); the title is ≤ 35 characters, the same in the game and on the form, not a common word or someone else's name (E_TITLE_GENERIC).
- Full Launch: land new players in gameplay at once, at most 1 click; text legible at devicePixelRatio 1 in 821×462 and 800×450 frames; no custom fullscreen button; Esc and Ctrl+W are not game keys (use e.code, so WASD is ZQSD on AZERTY).
- Works with mouse and touch on desktop and mobile browsers (Chrome, Edge); no right-click menu; no text selection.
- Saves go through the SDK data module (cloud-synced for logged-in players) — automatic.
- No external links, no other portals' branding, no login walls.

### `web` — Web (own site, portals)

HTML5 build for a website or a web game portal.

- Platform: web; ads: none; purchases: no; privacy policy: optional
- No ads and no purchases yet: a portal SDK becomes another ad provider when a game needs it.
